picks.excerpt: A Spoken-commissioned survey found 61% of listeners mistook AI narration for human voices and the same share favored AI narration in multi-character scenes, even as a separate Audio Publishers Association study showed overall willingness to try AI-narrated audiobooks slipping year over year.
picks.rationale: Strongest of the audiobook cluster: PW is the most authoritative trade outlet and the concrete survey figures directly inform how audiobook producers and indie authors weigh AI narration for multi-cast titles.

picks.excerpt: Creative Access's 2026 'Thrive' report finds publishing has the lowest AI uptake of any creative industry at just 6%, reflecting ongoing concerns around copyright and authorship even as adjacent creative sectors adopt AI tools far faster.
picks.rationale: Distinct benchmark story from a reputable trade source: the 6% uptake figure gives publishing professionals a hard data point on where their industry sits versus other creative sectors.

picks.excerpt: Robert Moor argues publishing faces a growing 'hologram problem': AI summarizers, chat tools, marketing blurbs and podcasts now convey a book's substance so convincingly that readers increasingly consume the simulacrum instead of reading the book itself, reshaping how titles are written, sold and read.
picks.rationale: Distinct, forward-looking argument on AI summary/chat tools displacing actual reading — reframes how editors and marketers think about discoverability and the value of the book itself, from a credible literary outlet.

dropped.reason: Same story as the kept Publishers Weekly pick — 'AI multi-cast audiobook narration acceptance.' Per the same-story rule the audiobook cluster collapses to a single card; PW is the stronger, more authoritative source.

Derivative of the same audiobook-narration survey story — the Self-Publishing with Dale podcast simply breaks down the survey data covered by the PW/Jane Friedman items. Collapsed into the single kept audiobook card.
